aws-iam-example.note: AWS publishes this on its IAM pages. aws-placeholder drops it.

aws-sts-example.note: The same value on the STS pages. GitHub alerted on it anyway, which is why the vectors file exists.

aws-secret-access-key.note: The secret AWS prints beside the example key ID. No shipped rule matches an AWS secret; the entropy floor is measured on it.

aws-iam-example-second-body.note: A second published example. Same suffix, different body, so a suffix check and a table disagree here.

aws-access-key-id.note: Fabricated. A long-term key ID that survives every check the rule applies.

aws-session-key-id.note: Fabricated. The same, on the prefix STS issues.

aws-bearer-token-id.note: Fabricated. The ABIA prefix, which the inherited rule matches and nothing here has traced to a document AWS publishes.

aws-context-credential-id.note: Fabricated. The ACCA prefix, on the same footing as ABIA.

aws-example-at-head.note: Fabricated. EXAMPLE at the head of the body, which a suffix check must not drop.

aws-example-in-middle.note: Fabricated. EXAMPLE inside the body, same reason.

google-api-key.note: Fabricated. A Google API key that clears its rule's entropy floor, used by internal/selftest to produce a block from a rule that is not the canary's.

aws-access-key-id-utf16le.note: The key planted/aws-access-key-id-utf16le.env is built around, in its own entry because a fixture sharing a literal makes every edit to one a silent break in the other. Carries the project's name so it can be found; no EXAMPLE suffix.

anthropic-api-key.note: Fabricated, and marked 0SPILLGUARD. The shape gitleaks and TruffleHog both match: 93 bytes and a closing AA. The boundary tests in internal/scan vary it from here.

anthropic-admin-api-key.note: The same body length behind the admin prefix, so that arm of the alternation is driven apart from the other.

us-ssn.note: Area 666 is one the Social Security Administration has never issued, so this cannot be anyone's number, and us-ssn refuses only the 900s, so it is still found.
